email.body1:
Brandi, saw Teamworks crossed a $1.5B valuation and just folded PFF's enterprise business into the platform.

Growth and acquisitions like that usually open more in-market accounts than business development can cover before new reps ramp, and that is where deals stall. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Teamworks off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Brandi, quick follow-up for Teamworks.

After raises and acquisitions, pipeline targets tend to jump faster than headcount can keep up. Most teams cannot say how many meetings they actually need to hit the new number, so the gap surfaces late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Teamworks needs to cover this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Brandi, last bit of proof for Teamworks.

Memgraph had more accounts in play than the team could touch and could not hire fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Teamworks' reply rate likely compares to other high-growth software companies. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?

Brandi, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling business development without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing is everything during a fast integration period, and I know acquisition season is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I will tailor it to Teamworks either way.
